#4058. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 13, 2026

Today is Friday the 13th, but let's not dwell on that. Here are some weekend video games to play. Well, actually, here are some of our biggest stories of the week, and then you can check out some weekend game recommendations.

Also, go ahead and make some space on your Xbox or PlayStation hard drive to make room for GTAVI. It's going to be about 200 GB and you can pre-load it now. Delete those games you're not going to return to. Delete all those video clips you'll never watch from every time you get a Trophy on your PlayStation. And you know what? Go ahead and delete Fortnite, too. It's time.

Calling all sickos of The Rootrees Are Dead, Return of the Obra Dinn, The Incident At Galley House, and everything in between: there’s another good deduction game to obsess over. Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.

NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.

Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.

Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.

It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.

Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.

You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.

As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on current platforms with modernized improvements to boot.

If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.

I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.

FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.

Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.

If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

#4057. GTA 6 Already Has 2.5 Million Twitch Viewers

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

The last 30 minutes have been, quite frankly, massive for the world of video games. Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews dropped, and it's officially the highest-rated game ever released. The review embargo coincided with the game's release in New Zealand, as midnight struck in that territory. Players are now starting to get their hands on the game.

While some are opting to take "sneaky flights," changing the time on their consoles to gain access to it early, others have just opted to passively view things. Within 30 minutes, the game has broken the Twitch record for the most-viewed single-player game of all time, and it's undoubtedly about to break the most-viewed game record imminently.

Before today, according to Guinness World Records, the most-viewed single-player game of all time on Twitch peaked at 1,280,000. That was Hogwarts Legacy, back in 2023. 30 minutes after launch, Grand Theft Auto 6 obliterated that record.

As of right now, there are over 2.5 million viewers in the GTA 6 category on Twitch, each one itching to get an early view of what the game contains. Streamer Alanzoka has 227,000 viewers alone, and others like xQc and TheBurntPeanut have 99,000 and 48,000, respectively.

The multiplayer record looks set to tumble shortly. According to TwitchTracker, League of Legends holds the record for the most concurrent viewers for a multiplayer game, peaking at 3,111,023 back in November 2022. Grand Theft Auto 6 is 80 percent of the way there, and half of the United States, Twitch's biggest audience, is still asleep. Valorant holds the record for most viewing hours in a single day at 34 million, but there's almost no chance it'll hold on, with GTA likely to smash it today.

Prior to release, the game was already breaking records, becoming the most preordered game in history, with at least 10 million preorders. That was nine days before release, so that almost certainly doubled. If you're planning to play at midnight in your local time, just make sure you follow PlayStation's latest piece of mandatory advice.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4056. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4055. Something Weird Is Going On With GoldenEye 007 And Xbox Game Pass

Earlier this month, you may recall that Xbox announced 14 games that would be leaving Game Pass in early November, with arguably the highlight of the bunch being the classic Rare FPS, GoldenEye 007.

We initially thought this might have been a mistake, but then Xbox doubled-down by announcing the game's departure in an official Xbox Wire roundup, confirming that it would definitely be leaving console and cloud on November 15th.

We're now on November 16th, and GoldenEye 007 remains included with Game Pass. Every other title from the list has been removed from the service, but Bond has defied the odds once again to remain part of the subscription!

So, what's going on here? It might take a while until we find out for sure, but we're going to guess that Xbox has either managed to arrange a deal to keep GoldenEye 007 on Game Pass, or they've just pushed back the removal date.

In any case, it's weird that nobody's said anything about this yet, and we're hoping we'll get clarification in the near future. GoldenEye has always been a game that's been tied up in licensing issues (hence why we never got the cancelled Xbox 360 version of it), but perhaps they've managed to figure out a long-term solution.

Anyway, we'll keep an eye on it, and this article will be updated with any important information that's revealed over the next few days. For now though, feel free to keep enjoying GoldenEye 007 on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and Premium!

#4053. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4052. Sea Of Stars Is Getting A 'Sunset Edition' Switch 2 Physical And A Gorgeous Final Merch Drop

Sabotage Studio's Sea of Stars is no stranger to a physical release or merch drop, and today, iam8bit has announced that it has one final collection in store.

A brand new Switch 2 physical, the Sea of Stars: Sunset Edition ($49.99), is the star of the show, launching on 2nd April 2027. This one packs the full game and all of its expansions on the cartridge (what a concept!), and comes with some sweet sticker sheets and a download code for the game's soundtrack.

There's a beefier option in the Exclusive Edition, which also boasts an exclusive sleeve and an in-box manual, for those after a little throwback.

The beefiest of the bunch, mind you, is still to come. The Collector's Edition contains all of the goodies outlined above, and throws in a bunch of extra merch too. We're talking a double-sided poster, a tote bag, a reversible bandana, a Rainbow Conch keychain, and seven pins, all housed in a Rainbow Conch Chest. Come on, that's sweet.

The Collector's Edition comes in at a pricey $129.99 (or you can just get the merch for $79.99). All of the above are now available to pre-order from the iam8bit website until 11th January, before shipping in April.

As if all of that wasn't enough, iam8bit has also announced that it has two vinyl LPs in the pipeline, one all about the main game soundtrack, and one featuring the tunes from the Throes of the Watchmaker DLC. You'll also find pre-order information about these on the iam8bit site.

#4051. Cleanser Man Is Mega Man: Dual Override’s Boss Design Contest Winner

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.  To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

#4050. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4048. How Wuthering Waves Brings Its Evolving World to Life Through Character Design, Music and Storytelling

This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, Kuro Games.

Solaris-3 is a world still recovering from the Lament, a cataclysm that reshaped its land and left Tacet Discords roaming the ruins. Players enter it as the Rover, a wanderer with no memory, and rebuild their understanding of the world one region at a time.

Since launch, that world has grown far beyond its starting point in Huanglong. Rinascita, Lahai-Roi and now the Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou in Version 3.7 have each added new cultures, new Resonators and new mysteries to uncover. Version 3.8 sets the stage for the next major chapter, paving the way for Version 4.0 and the arrival of the New Federation.

But Wuthering Waves does more than add new places and faces. It gives every addition meaning through three connected creative pillars: character design, music and storytelling. Together, they turn new content into something players feel, not just something they unlock.

In Wuthering Waves, a Resonator's outfit is a passport. Costume, color, silhouette and animation tell you where a character comes from and what role they play, often before they say a word.

The clearest example is Rinascita, whose cast looks like it belongs to a single, coherent culture while each member stays distinct:

If the costume introduces a character, animation brings them to life. Jinhsi, the Magistrate of Jinzhou, moves with poised, ceremonial grace that suits a leader. The Shorekeeper's calm, drifting motions reflect her role as a quiet guardian of the Black Shores. Even an Intro Skill becomes a small character beat.

Each new region gives Kuro Games a new artistic direction to explore, from Huanglong's flowing robes to Rinascita's carnival and gladiator styles, and on to the tribal and futuristic looks of Lahai-Roi. The cast grows more varied with every update, yet still reads as one world.

If character design tells you who belongs where, music tells you how it feels to be there. The soundtrack's strength comes down to three ideas: genre fusion, musical world building and lyrics that tell stories.

Wuthering Waves rarely sticks to a single genre. A track might set its mood with synthesizers and programmed drums, then hand the melody to strings, piano or electric guitar. Cartethyia's "With Glory I Shall Fall" blends orchestral instruments with synth bass and electric guitar: the orchestra brings grandeur, while the guitar and bass add urgency and a modern edge. The mix is deliberate, matching a world where ancient tradition and advanced technology sit side by side.

The soundtrack changes its musical vocabulary as you travel. The music of Huanglong is anchored by sweeping melodies and traditional instrumental timbres, creating a tranquil yet deeply narrative atmosphere. Rinascita’s soundtrack is brighter and more vibrant, blending romanticism with dramatic tension—echoing the seaport city-state’s rich artistic heritage. Meanwhile, Lahai-Roi leans toward a modern pop aesthetic, complementing its science-fiction, academic setting. You can sense a region's identity through its music before you know its history.

Vocal tracks are part of the storytelling, not decoration. Phrolova's theme, "Reveries in the Crimson Beyond", speaks to a dream as if asking it for comfort and company, reflecting her longing to stay inside an imagined world and hold on to moments she has lost. Players who know her story hear the lyrics differently, and the song in turn deepens their understanding of her.

The emotional power of Wuthering Waves’ music does not end when players leave the game. Through To the New World, the game’s first global concert tour, its music travelled from the virtual world into reality, visiting six cities—Shanghai, Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei, Singapore and Los Angeles—and attracting nearly 50,000 attendees worldwide. Blending orchestral performances, live vocals, band arrangements and immersive stage productions, the concert brought familiar melodies and character themes to life in new ways. It also rekindled memories of pivotal story moments and beloved characters, giving players the chance to relive those emotions together and experience a second emotional resonance with the game.

That commitment has also earned industry recognition. After “Against the Tide” won the 2025 HMMA for Song – Video Game (Console & PC), Wuthering Waves received three more nominations in 2026—across original song, mobile-game music and live concert performance. These honors reflect how the game treats music not merely as accompaniment, but as the emotional heartbeat of its characters and world.

The world of Wuthering Waves feels alive because its story never stops moving. Characters change, conflicts shift, and places carry the marks of what happened there.

The Rover's search for lost memories is the thread that runs through every region. Each Main Quest chapter pulls the Rover deeper into the mysteries of the Lament and the forces shaping Solaris-3, giving players a reason to keep moving forward.

The larger plot matters because the people in it do. Character-related quests explore what drives each Resonator: their loyalties, their losses and the choices they struggle with. When a Resonator you know steps into a Main Quest, the stakes feel personal.

Each region introduces its own culture, politics and conflicts. Huanglong wrestles with duty and protection, Rinascita with faith and tradition, and Lahai-Roi with knowledge and the future. Version 3.7 brought the Xuanfang arc to its finale in the Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou.

Not every story is told in dialogue. Ruined cities, overgrown battlefields and quiet landmarks hint at the history behind them, rewarding players who explore and look closely.

Every major update adds a new chapter of history, a new set of characters and a new storyline. Instead of a fixed world, Solaris-3 is one that keeps changing alongside the people who live in it.

Wuthering Waves is at its best when design, music and story work as one, and nearly every Resonator in the cast is built this way. Here are three examples of how it works.

Design. Cartethyia’s dual-form design brings her past and present together. Her Cartethyia form reflects the free wandering knight she has become, while Fleurdelys recalls the Blessed Maiden, vessel of Divinity and Queen of Gale and Tide she once was. Fate bestowed upon her the title of the Blessed Maiden, but it was her own choices that gave the title its true meaning.

Music. Her theme, "With Glory I Shall Fall", mirrors that duality. Orchestral grandeur speaks to the legend of the Blessed Maiden, while electric guitar and synth bass bring the force of the warrior who fights for Rinascita.

Story. Her story gives both of them meaning. Once you learn how the title of Blessed Maiden came to rest on her shoulders, her two forms and her theme stop being separate details and become one character.

None of the three would land as hard alone. Together, they make Cartethyia unforgettable.

Design. One of Aemeath's most distinctive design features is the transformation between her human and mech forms. The mech is a transformation form born from her past as an Exostrider Synchronist, as well as an extension of her own abilities. Elements of Fleet Snowfluff's design are also incorporated into the mech, making it both a reflection of her childhood admiration for heroes and an essential means through which she fights and protects others. The seamless transitions between her two forms, along with their cooperative combat, further reinforce the connection between them.

Music. As the digital songstress known as Fleet Snowfluff, music plays an integral role in Aemeath's characterization. In her character teaser, Memories of Fleet Snowfluff, we see her wholeheartedly practicing her songs. Her voice fits perfectly with Lahai-Roi's contemporary pop-inspired musical style. More notably, the development team uses forward and reversed versions of the same melody to represent different timelines, connecting Aemeath's childhood and adult selves through a shared musical motif. As the truth behind her story gradually unfolds, players come to realize that these melodies had been quietly foreshadowing the emotional revelations all along.

Story. If her design and music bring Aemeath's character to life, then the Version 3.1 Main Quest reveals the reasons behind these creative choices. She was once an Exostrider Synchronist at Startorch Academy, and an ordinary girl with dreams of her own. However, after resonating with the Exostrider and pushing herself into Overclock, she lost her physical body and became a digital ghost. Her encounters with Rover also form a causal loop centered on connection, memory, and protection.

Design. Hsin is the Sentinel of Mengzhou and the first playable Sentinel. In combat she splits into fox forms, a striking image for a guardian who is more than she first appears.

Music. Her theme, "Ode to Hsin and Moon", is a vocal song composed by Jin Dazhou and sung by Jaime Arin. It comes in two versions, "Endless Yearning" and "Whither Away?", and the titles alone give her two moods: a longing that never fades, and a question of where her path will lead.

Story. Version 3.7 closes the Xuanfang arc around her. Her storyline completes the logical loop of her audiovisual design: it unveils why her character design highlights power while her music reflects an inner uncertainty, bringing both sides into unity through her story.

Three regions, three very different Resonators, yet in each one design, music and story point the same way. That harmony is what makes the world of Wuthering Waves feel alive.

Wuthering Waves keeps growing, but size is not what makes Solaris-3 memorable. What sets it apart is how each new region and Resonator arrives fully realized: dressed in a look that belongs to their culture, carried by music that gives them an emotional voice, and woven into a story that connects them to everything around them.

Through Version 3.7, that approach has taken players from the halls of Jinzhou to the carnival streets of Rinascita, the frontiers of Lahai-Roi and the heart of Xuanfang. With Version 3.8 now live, Rovers will find their paths crossing more and more with the New Federation. A new story is about to set off from here. Wherever the Rover heads next, one thing seems certain: the next chapter of Solaris-3 will be worth seeing, hearing and feeling.

#4047. 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

#4046. Splatoon 3 Version 12.0.0 Update Out Now, Here Are The Full Patch Notes

The dev team also has another update on the way

Update [Wed 18th Nov 2026, 12:05am]: This new update for Splatoon 3 (Version 12.0.0) is now officially available to download. You can see the patch notes below.

Original Story: Nintendo's team-based squid-shooter Splatoon 3 is still going strong, and this week the title is getting updated to Version 12.0.0.

This major update will come with changes to multiplayer, including weapon adjustments. There are also changes to Anarchy Battle, X Battles and challenges. Additionally, there are changes to the GameChat feature on Switch 2. Nintendo also notes how its next update after this one will focus on multiplayer game balance.

You can get the full rundown in the official patch notes below (via Nintendo's official support page):

On this page: Splatoon 3 - Version 12.0.0 (17th November 2026)

Sections marked "on Nintendo Switch 2" apply only to Nintendo Switch 2. All other changes apply to both Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch.

Made it possible to participate with a friend in traditional X Battles as a group of two.

Added a feature that allows players to open GameChat and invite friends from their group while playing modes with friends, such as battles or Salmon Run.

This update focuses on making changes to matchmaking and multiplayer balance.

For X Battles, we have added a feature to allow players to play as a pair with a friend. The goal of this feature is to expand the range of ways to play, and we will introduce it on a trial basis starting in Chill Season 2026. After we have introduced it, we will comprehensively analyze how these battles are actually played and how the gameplay situation shifts, including for players who are not playing with a friend. Then we will decide whether to continue providing this feature in future seasons.

For Anarchy Battle (Series), we have changed the matchmaking system such that, in exchange for removing the feature allowing players to continue with the same team, matchmaking will now complete more quickly and with less imbalance of skill level and equipped weapons between players and their opponents.

For Challenges, we have changed how Challenge Power is calculated to make it easier to raise Challenge Power the more wins a player has. With this change, between players who would have ended up with about the same Challenge Power under the previous system, the player who attained the greater number of wins will have the higher final Challenge Power.

For multiplayer balance, we made a variety of changes to main, sub, and special weapons, including changes to the flight distance of Blaster shots.

With most weapons, when a player fires while moving, the player's movement speed is added to the shot's speed to a certain extent, resulting in a more natural trajectory. For Blasters, we have minimized the change in shot flight distance caused by this effect, making it easier to maintain an appropriate distance against an opponent’s Blaster.

Among the special weapons, we have changed the Reefslider because, while there is statistically little impact on victories in matches between extremely skilled players, it has a high impact on matches between less skilled players. The intention behind this change is to alleviate that striking difference. By narrowing the area affected by the explosion we have made it so that players cannot reap the maximum benefit without using it at the precise position. On the other hand, we have extended the invulnerability period to make it harder for opponents who used terrain to survive the explosion to counterattack and easier for the player to make follow-up attacks.

For the Tenta Missiles, we have decreased the vulnerability while firing and expanded the area where it is possible to lock on to opponents. As a result, it will now be easier to use, even in situations where opponents are nearby the player. By decreasing the impact interval, it becomes easier to defeat opponents who are slow to dodge, but the duration for which they must keep dodging is reduced.

We have also added a feature for Nintendo Switch 2 that will make it easier to use GameChat.

The next update will focus on changes to multiplayer balance.

If you haven't already played the game on Switch 2, there's a free upgrade available which includes visual improvements and frame rate optimisations for the platform. In some related news, Splatoon Raiders has also received an eShop demo this week!

#4045. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

#4044. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4041. GTA 6 Doesn’t Have The Internet Because It Wasn’t “Necessary”

Grand Theft Auto games are time capsules, and I'm not just talking about the anachronistic entries like Vice City that unravel the glitz and seedy glamour of '80s Miami movies.

Between sending mob bosses to swim with the fish and bowling with his cousin in GTA 4, Niko Bellic visits an internet café to chat with women online. The entire interface is a relic of early naughties forums and crude online shopping, something that GTA 5 would iterate on and bring to mobile. Part of making the game world feel real meant tackling the online world, and Rockstar understood that—right down to emailing, an infamous LCPD sting operation, and in-game news sites. GTA 6, however, is bucking that trend, getting rid of the internet entirely for something much more 2026.

In an interview with Kotaku ahead of the game's launch, Rockstar explained why it removed the internet, and why in-game social media was a better fit for Leonida; "It didn't feel necessary for us," head of development Rob Nelson said. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps."

Nelson assured that just because GTA 6 doesn't have an in-game internet to browse, that doesn't mean the idea won't return in the future—and Rockstar has hinted that sequels won't take nearly as long to get out the door. But for Leonida, the team wanted players to experience the "meaningful stuff" by focusing on the open world, rather than navigating an interface on their phones. They wanted you to fixate on "doing Grand Theft Auto," engaging with the world's economics and systems instead of mindlessly online shopping for lavish cars.

It's taken approximately 35 minutes for GTA 6 to start breaking records.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of sh*t, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," he continued. "It was never a top-down, 'We're not going to have websites.' I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it."

Jason and Lucia won't bumble into a sting operation, and you can't order an Oppressor from your phone, but the in-game social media app Snapmatic—Rockstar's answer to Instagram. It has entire feeds with actual pages and posts, so a lot of work has gone into making the online side of GTA 6's world feel as alive and realistic as past entries, just with the focus shifted entirely to social media instead of car dealerships and pyramid schemes.

The most anticipated video game of all time is a triumph on every level that exceeds years of unbelievable expectations. You're not ready for Leonida.

#4038. Xbox CEO Pens New Message, Urges Platform Not To Get 'Trapped' By Its Proud History

Yesterday, we talked about the Project Helix part of the Xbox 25th anniversary magazine that's been made available to read in full on the official Xbox Wire website, and there's plenty more interesting stuff where that came from!

For example, the magazine kicks off with a statement from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who discusses the past 25 years of the brand and where it's going in the future - similar to a statement she shared on social media recently.

This time though, she talks less about how games will be made, and more about the fact that she wants to take "creative risks" while also acknowledging that her team won't "get every decision right" along the way.

"There are plenty of milestones from the past 25 years, and you'll find many of them in these pages. But I don't think the story of Xbox is really a story about any given hardware, launch or number. It is a story about people. Players turned games into friendships, rivalries and family traditions. They played with roommates who became lifelong friends, with brothers and sisters who moved across the country, with parents who got older and kids who eventually picked up the controller themselves. Some of the people we played with 25 years ago are no longer here. Some are sitting next to us, now playing with a new generation."

"We should be proud of that history. But we shouldn't be trapped by it."

"Games are alive. The best ones find new players and new creators. They move between generations. They get changed, remade and occasionally broken apart and rebuilt into something nobody expected. Twenty-five years in, Xbox should have that same restlessness."

"We have been given the chance to care for some of the most loved games and characters in the world. Our job is to protect what makes them special without protecting them from change. To keep making new things. To take creative risks. To meet players wherever they choose to play. And to make sure someone discovering Xbox for the first time today can feel the same possibility that someone felt turning on that first console in 2001."

"We don't get every decision right. No company that is still making things does. But we can keep listening, learning and building. Twenty-five years ago, a relatively small group of people imagined that Microsoft could make a game console. It was an improbable idea. They made it real. I like that as our inheritance."

There's definitely some interesting stuff in here, including Sharma's insistence that Xbox shouldn't be "trapped" by its past, that her team should be willing to experiment and take risks in the future, and an admission that not every decision will work out for the best. That's pretty refreshing to hear, and it certainly reads well on paper at least.

Let's see what happens, eh? Xbox's 25th anniversary has been a weird year, full of ups and downs, but it seems like there's a cautious optimism circulating around the fanbase regarding things like console updates, exclusives and various other initiatives that have been introduced since the Xbox CEO took the helm at the start of the year.

These next 25 years are going to be fascinating to say the least!

#4037. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

#4036. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#4034. Pokémon Champions Is Getting A Balance Patch Next Month

The Pokémon Company has announced the free-to-play Switch and mobile game Pokémon Champions is getting a balance update next month on 2nd December 2026.

This balance update will include move updates and adjustments. Here's the rundown about the moves certain Pokémon will now have access to. Along with this are details about the adjustments to select moves (via Nintendo Everything).

The following Pokémon will be able to use the moves listed here

Psych Up: Alakazam, Starmie, Mr. Mime, Mawile, Altaria, Castform, Absol, Roserade, Weavile, Rotom, Rotom (Heat Rotom), Rotom (Wash Rotom), Rotom (Frost Rotom), Rotom (Fan Rotom), Rotom (Mow Rotom), Liepard, Musharna, Audino, Cofagrigus, Slurpuff, Drampa, Annihilape

Play Rough: Vaporeon, Jolteon, Flareon, Espeon, Umbreon, Leafeon, Glaceon

Adjustments will be made to the following moves Screech: 85% → 100% accuracy Rock Slide: 90% → 95% accuracy, 30% → 20% chance to make targets flinch Steel Wing: 90% → 100% accuracy Metal Sound: 85% → 100% accuracy Frost Breath: 90% → 100% accuracy

Adjustments will be made to the following Abilities Flash Fire: When the Ability Flash Fire is activated, the Pokémon now gains the Fire Boost status. The Fire Boost status will persist even if the Pokémon Mega Evolves.

Stalwart: The Pokémon ignores the effects of Abilities and moves that draw in moves. ↓ The Pokémon ignores the effects of Abilities and moves that draw in moves. When using its moves, the Pokémon ignores the effects of targets’ substitutes.

This balance patch announcement follows the release of Z Mega Evolutions in Champions in September. You can find out more about this and Pokémon Champions in general, in our previous coverage here on Nintendo Life:

#4033. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#4032. Half-Life: Alyx Was Officially Announced 7 Years Ago Today

Valve has a penchant for making the biggest, boldest announcements, with the fanfare of a local bus route confirming cancellations. "We're excited to unveil Half-Life: Alyx, our flagship VR game, this Thursday." That's how the first Half-Life game in over a decade was announced.

No trailer, not even a screenshot, a tweet. And it worked. I vividly remember seeing that post while scrolling my feed and almost leaping out of my chair. The long-rumored HLVR was real. It hadn't been canceled without a peep from Valve like so many iterations before it. The dry streak had ended and Half-Life was back.

I hate to make you feel old, and remind you of the brutal passage of time, but that announcement was 7 years ago today—over half the length between Episode Two and Alyx.

So, where's Half-Life 3? The powder keg felt as though it was finally going to blow last October, and then last November, and then last December, and then... poof. It was a dud. No news, no Half-Life 3, and silence from Valve. Mike Shapiro's cryptic 2025 new year's tease led to nothing. The HLX leaks and confident reports from everyone, not just the usual leakers, fell flat. And now, fans are wary of jumping on the hopium train again lest they fall into a Citadel core of disappointment.

By all accounts, Valve did intend to unveil HLX, widely believed to be Half-Life 3, but delayed its plans because something was "not up to snuff." Whatever that something was, we don't know, but it was enough that timelines got completely pushed back. Fans are again convinced that Geoff Keighley, posting his usual anniversary celebrations, is teasing HLX at The Game Awards, but given Valve's unceremonious Twitter announcements in the past, that's incredibly unlikely. What we do know is that Half-Life 3 hasn't been canceled, as an employee outright mentioned HLX during a livestream.

Although it doesn't completely change the game, Half-Life: Alyx sets a new standard for quality that will unquestionably make a huge impact on VR.

Mike Morasky said during the stream that "HLX has its own version" of Deadlock's HDR system, to which his coworker muttered, "nice work." Half-Life 3 hasn't gone the way of... well, Half-Life 3. It still exists, and dataminers continue to find evidence that it's being worked on. Considering it was an internal delay and not an outright cancelation and reboot, we probably won't be waiting another 7 years for Valve to announce it, even if 2026 ends without a whiff of confirmation.

In late October, reputable Valve leaker Tyler McVicker, who held his ground on 'HLVR' right up until Alyx was confirmed on November 18, 2019, uncovered all sorts of new strings—Hammer map editor enhancements, Combine gunships with bomb targets, and even a surge of activity surrounding the game. Gabe Follower claimed just last week that Valve had added new rendering functionality to Counter-Strike 2, including parallax occlusion mapping and frost effects. These were used for the new winter-themed Cobblestone, but could easily be doubled up on for HLX, given that Episode Two's cliffhanger ends with Gordon Freeman set for an expedition to the Arctic in search of the Borealis.

So, it's been 7 years since Alyx was announced, and 6 years since Alyx launched. To answer the question, 'Where is Half-Life 3?' It's being worked on behind closed doors in complete secrecy, with the occasional slip-up from devs on livestreams confirming its existence, while dataminers rip out whatever references they can from the innards of its development. It's real. It hasn't been canceled. That could always change, but for now, there's reason to be optimistic. Hopefully, one day soon, we'll have an announcement that we can look back on in 7 years' time just like this.

#4031. Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff

Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations.

#4030. 'We've Heard You!' - Star Wars Galactic Racer Is Officially Adding Split-Screen Multiplayer

An incredible addition to an incredible game

Star Wars Galactic Racer is my favourite game of the year so far. It's an incredible racing title that even surpasses the original Star Wars Episode 1 Racer in my view, and I've had so much fun with the campaign and online multiplayer.

There's just one downside that everyone's been pointing out since it was revealed, and that's the absence of local split-screen multiplayer. With that in mind, the development team have found a way to implement it in a new update.

The update isn't available yet, but will be coming to the game in early 2027. Alongside it will be a new mode called Free Play, which is where you'll be able to freely choose your vehicle, character, planet and race track.

"We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action."

It seems Free Play is the only place where you'll be able to access local split-screen multiplayer in Star Wars Galactic Racer, but that's no surprise considering how solo-focused the main campaign is. They'd literally have to rewrite massive portions of the campaign if they were going to implement split-screen into it.

Anyway, this is just an amazing bonus on top of an already amazing game, and I encourage you to check it out if you enjoy a title like Burnout 3: Takedown - it's fast-paced and frantic, has the same kind of takedown system that you'll remember from that game, and the roguelite campaign is really well designed (online is great fun as well).

If you've played it, let us know what you think of the game in the poll down below!

#4029. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.
